stepNotes.1: The server unit composes authentication, origin checks, rate limiting, directory scoping, route groups, Unix-socket IPC, and mDNS while retaining thin facades for shared runtime contracts.
stepNotes.2: Untrusted network, path, configuration, and browser-origin inputs are constrained before domain calls; secrets are redacted and non-loopback publication is gated by authenticated-bind policy.
stepNotes.3: Error envelopes, IPC request parsing, project-scoped audit and event filtering, canonical worktree removal, and durable autonomous transitions are explicit; the legacy 403 error name remains semantically inconsistent.
stepNotes.4: SSE queues, reconnect delay, audit exports, context checks, and rate buckets are bounded, while the unsigned IPC frame length remains an uncapped local robustness concern.
stepNotes.5: Transport, framing, directory admission, normalization, redaction, context discovery, and route translation have clear ownership, with message-pattern error classification the main coupling pressure.
stepNotes.6: Fallback catches are mostly deliberate and documented; two cleanup catches still suppress cancellation or WebSocket-close diagnostics and match the deferred Low ledger item.
stepNotes.7: Focused coverage is strong for route validation, redaction, IPC flow, DRE escaping, audit filtering, and autonomous durability but omits oversized IPC frames, live event backpressure, mDNS failures, and several context-check ecosystems.
stepNotes.8: Independent evidence supports retaining AUDIT-server-empty-catch as Low and deferred; neither ledger content nor source inspection identified a Critical item requiring a reverify artifact.
stepNotes.9: Core typechecking passed and all 123 tests across 11 selected server files passed after the IPC suite was rerun with permission to create its temporary Unix socket.
